classification.difficultyReason: Combine two three-year compound-growth factors and convert the combined multiplier to a percentage increase.

content.prompt: A doctor took out a six-year loan to start a medical practice. For the first three years, he was charged compound interest at a rate of $9\%$ p.a. For the second three-year period, he was charged compound interest at a rate of $13\%$ p.a. Find the total percentage increase in the money owing, correct to the nearest $1\%$.

answer.short:
$87\%$ increase.

Multiply the two three-year growth factors, then subtract $1$ and multiply by $100\%$.
answer.worked:
Let $P$ be the original loan amount.

$$\begin{align*}A_3&=P(1.09)^3\\A_6&=P(1.09)^3(1.13)^3\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage increase}&=\bigl((1.09)^3(1.13)^3-1\bigr)\times100\%\\\text{Percentage increase}&=86.8593459013\%\\\text{Percentage increase}&\approx87\%\end{align*}$$

The money owing increased by $87\%$, correct to the nearest $1\%$.
